parsed.title: Allowlist order contradicts ROUTING's 'router runs first'
parsed.detail: SKILL.md progressive loading lists the replan check as item 4, 'Only when node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN> prints route: replan: load the replan contract', after the redirect gate (1), planning preflight (2) and phase contract (3). But references/ROUTING.md mandates 'Before the status gate, run node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>' — i.e. before item 1's gates. The same file cannot both run the router first (ROUTING.md) and only consult it after the preflight/phase-contract loads (SKILL.md item 4).

parsed.title: 'Both resources are normative' stale after allowlist grew to four
parsed.detail: The diff replaces the two-path allowlist with four items (adding planning-preflight and the replan contract) but keeps the closing sentence 'Do not load planning gates after a redirect stop. Both resources are normative, one hop from this file, and fail closed when missing.' — 'Both' no longer matches the four-item allowlist it now follows.

parsed.title: Replan exemption contradicts plan-fix's own turn contract and hand-off
parsed.detail: Item 7 says on route: replan the phases are 'appended to the unit's existing SPEC ledger on the same branch instead of a new fix SPEC'. But the Turn contract requires 'The fix SPEC is committed on its fix/<n>-<topic> branch (commit sha pasted)', 'Both ledgers are frozen in the SPEC', and the fixed Hand-off block 'SPEC drafted: docs/fix/<primary>-<topic>/SPEC.md … → Next: /review-plan fix-<primary>'. On the replan route no new SPEC/branch/commit exists, so the turn contract and hand-off cannot be satisfied and no exemption is carved for them; the Hard rule 'create fix/<n>-<topic> first, never main' also still applies unconditionally.

parsed.title: Router 'before ingest' is unexecutable ordering
parsed.detail: The new paragraph says to run the router 'before ingest' when 'the target resolves to an existing unit folder', but the unit folder (docs/fix/<n>-<topic>) is only known after step 1 ingests and resolves the numeric issue tokens; and SKILL.md item 7 places the router check after drafting steps 2–6. Both orderings make the 'run first, do not draft a new fix SPEC' instruction impossible to honor as written.

parsed.title: Replan trigger duplicates the decision unit-route.mjs owns
parsed.detail: The new #224 bullet emits '{command: "/plan-feature <unit>" | "/plan-fix <issue>"…}' directly, while its own trigger text says this is 'the same class→destination decision scripts/unit-route.mjs owns'. Unit 224's contract (fold-findings, CLASSIFY.md, PERSIST_AND_DECIDE.md, triage-issue) is that the planner is named by the router's `route: replan` line, never re-derived by the caller; the sensor hardcodes the mapping anyway and its suggested entry never instructs running `node scripts/unit-route.mjs`, contradicting the single-sourcing claim in the same bullet.

parsed.title: Replan exemption bypasses the no-bypass Product-review gate without a receipt rule
parsed.detail: The exemption says a `route: replan` line means 'skip the STOP and load the replan contract' — but SKILL.md's guardrails state the Product-review gate 'has no bypass flag either' and the turn contract requires a current spec-review-pass receipt before any SPEC write. The exemption neither states whether the Product-review gate still runs on the replan path nor requires a receipt before appending phases, leaving a router-derived bypass of a gate declared bypass-free.

parsed.title: 'a router that cannot run is BLOCKED' — undefined verdict for this skill
parsed.detail: ROUTING.md introduces 'a router that cannot run is `BLOCKED`' (also PLANNING_PROCESS.md for plan-fix), but no BLOCKED output/verdict block is defined anywhere in plan-feature or plan-fix material; both skills' fail-closed paths print fixed STOP/hand-off blocks, so the mandated BLOCKED outcome has no contract.

parsed.title: Orphaned '(yes: …; no: omit this line)' in the fixed REVIEW-FAIL block
parsed.detail: In the REVIEW-FAIL `→ Next:` block the line '      (yes: <which box fired>; no: omit this line)' now appears after the two-cycle-cap paragraph, detached from the adversarial bullet it annotates ('…instead of single-reviewer' ends with no suffix). The file declares this block must be emitted 'verbatim, as multiple literal lines'; the printed block is structurally broken.
